name: Teamwork & Parliamentary Procedure

objectives.text: Describe ways team members take turns, share tasks, and listen to one another to complete a group project
Identify roles members can play on a team such as leader, recorder, timekeeper, and encourager
Explain how a group reaches a decision through discussion followed by a majority vote
Explain the purpose of parliamentary procedure in running an orderly meeting
Identify the FFA officer stations and the duties each officer performs during a chapter meeting
Identify the meaning of one, two, and three gavel taps used by a presiding officer
Describe the standard order of business for an FFA chapter meeting
Demonstrate how to make, second, and vote on a main motion
Define parliamentary terms such as motion, second, amendment, quorum, previous question, and adjourn
Explain how parliamentary procedure protects the rights of the majority, the minority, and absent members
Classify motions as main, subsidiary, privileged, incidental, or bringing a question again before the assembly and rank them by precedence
Record accurate minutes of a business meeting including each motion made and the result of each vote
Compare voting methods such as voice vote, rising vote, show of hands, and ballot and select the appropriate method for a meeting situation
Apply rules of debate including obtaining the floor, speaking limits, and germane discussion in a business meeting
Chair a short meeting that introduces, debates, and votes on a main motion
Analyze how a chapter committee divides its work and reports recommendations back to the full membership
Apply Robert's Rules of Order to process amendments, refer motions to committee, and raise points of order during a mock meeting
Analyze a meeting scenario to determine which motion is in order and whether it needs a second, is debatable, is amendable, and what vote it requires
Develop strategies to resolve conflict and keep team members engaged toward a shared chapter goal
Demonstrate parliamentary procedure as a team to resolve a chapter problem in the format of the FFA Parliamentary Procedure Career Development Event
Lead a chapter business meeting from call to order through adjournment using full parliamentary procedure
Evaluate the efficiency and fairness of a chapter meeting and recommend improvements to its procedures

changes: Kept all six existing objectives as real competencies, rewording a few for precision. Added teamwork roles, group decision making, FFA officer stations, gavel taps, order of business, parliamentary terms, member rights, motion classification and precedence, minutes, voting methods, debate rules, committee work, motion analysis, team conflict strategies, the Parliamentary Procedure CDE, and meeting evaluation. Standards are assigned only at grades 9 to 12 where an objective directly teaches the AFNR standard. Personal character, public speaking, and goal setting content was left to the sibling sub-topics.
